column1: # Remi AI development dataset. Steps in order.

column3: instruction
Dice the tomatoes and chili finely.
Stir into the mish with the olive oil; serve a little at a time with bread.
Spoon the molasses into a shallow dish.
Pour the tahini on top, swirl lightly and serve with bread.
Pour boiling water over the couscous, cover and leave 5 minutes.
Fluff with the melted butter.
Mix in sugar and raisins and top with coconut and nuts.
Use wheat that has been soaked overnight and boiled until very tender.
Simmer the cooked wheat in the milk with the sugar for 20 minutes, stirring.
Thicken with the corn starch dissolved in a little cold milk and boil 2 minutes; add vanilla.
Pour into a dish, cool and decorate with raisins, nuts and coconut.
Boil 350 g sugar with the water and lemon juice for 10 minutes to make syrup; cool.
Cook the milk, cream, corn starch and remaining sugar, stirring, into a thick cream; cool.
Pull the kunafa apart and rub with melted ghee.
Press half into a tray, spread the cream and cover with the rest.
Bake at 200 °C until deep golden; pour over the syrup and top with pistachios.
Bake the puff pastry until golden and break into pieces.
Spread the pastry, nuts, raisins and coconut in an ovenproof dish.
Heat the milk with sugar and vanilla and pour over.
Top with the cream and bake at 220 °C until bubbling and browned.
Beat the ghee with the powdered sugar until white and fluffy.
Add the vanilla and fold in the flour to a soft dough.
Shape into rings or balls and press a pistachio on top.
Bake at 160 °C until set but still pale.
Rinse the dried fruits.
Dissolve the sugar in the water and add the fruit.
Soak in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours; add nuts before serving.
Melt 100 g sugar with the water to a golden caramel and pour into a mould.
Warm the milk; whisk the eggs with remaining sugar and vanilla and stir in the milk.
Strain into the mould and bake in a water bath at 160 °C until set.
Chill well and turn out.
Boil 300 ml water with the butter, add the flour at once and stir until the dough leaves the pan.
Cool slightly and beat in the eggs one at a time with the vanilla.
Make a syrup from the sugar, remaining water and lemon; cool.
Pipe fingers into warm oil, raise the heat and fry until golden.
Drain and dip in the cold syrup.
Toast the semolina in butter until golden.
Heat the milk with sugar and add carefully (it will spit); stir until thick.
Press into a mould and decorate with nuts.
Warm the feteer in the oven.
Cut into pieces and serve with honey, cream or molasses.
Rinse the hibiscus.
Bring the water to a boil, add the hibiscus and simmer 5 minutes; steep 15 minutes.
Strain, sweeten with the sugar and serve hot or chilled.
Soak the rice in the water for 2 hours.
Blend the rice and water with the coconut until very smooth and strain.
Mix with cold milk, sugar and vanilla and chill well.
Peel two of the lemons; quarter all four and remove seeds.
Blend with mint, sugar and water, strain and serve over ice.
Brew strong tea.
Pour over mint leaves in glasses and sweeten.
Peel and cube the mangoes.
Blend with milk and sugar until smooth; serve cold.
Cut the guavas and blend with milk and sugar.
Strain to remove seeds and serve cold.
Put the fava beans and their liquid in a pot with the water and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Mash the beans lightly with a fork or masher, leaving some whole.
Crush the garlic with the salt and cumin and stir it into the beans with the lemon juice.
Spoon into bowls, drizzle with olive oil and top with diced tomato and chopped parsley if using.
Heat the fava beans with the water until simmering.
Mash coarsely and season with salt, cumin and lemon juice.
Serve topped with linseed oil and sliced chili.
Dice the onion, pepper and tomatoes; mince the garlic and chili.
Fry the onion and pepper in the oil until soft, then add garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook until saucy.
Stir in the fava beans with their liquid, cumin, salt and black pepper; simmer and mash lightly.
Finish with lemon juice and serve hot.
Heat the beans with half the water and mash.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, crushed garlic and the remaining water until smooth.
Stir most of the tahini into the beans with cumin and salt; top with the rest and the olive oil.
Soak the dried split fava beans in plenty of water overnight, then drain very well.
Mince the beans with the onion, leek, herbs, garlic and chili in a food processor until a fine green paste forms.
Mix in the cumin, ground coriander and salt; rest the mixture in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Just before frying, stir in the baking soda.
Shape into flat discs and press one side into sesame seeds if using.
Deep-fry in hot oil (about 175 °C) in batches until deep golden, 3 to 4 minutes per batch.
Drain on paper and serve hot with tahini sauce and bread.
Melt the butter in a frying pan and fry the basterma slices for 1 minute until fragrant.
Crack the eggs over the basterma and cook until the whites set.
Season with pepper (basterma is already salty) and serve.
Dice the onion, pepper and tomatoes.
Soften the onion and pepper in the oil, then add the tomatoes and cook down to a thick sauce.
Pour in the beaten eggs seasoned with salt, pepper and cumin and stir gently until just set.
Mash the cheese with a fork.
Dice the tomatoes and chili finely and fold into the cheese.
Dress with olive oil, lemon juice and dried mint.
Chop the onion, pepper and tomatoes; slice the garlic.
Fry the onion and pepper in olive oil until soft, then add garlic, cumin and paprika.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste; simmer until thick.
Make six wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook until the whites set.
Season and serve in the pan.
Peel the potatoes and cut into thin slices or fingers; rinse and dry thoroughly.
Fry in hot oil in batches until golden and crisp.
Drain and sprinkle with salt and cumin.
Grate the onion and chop the herbs finely.
Beat the eggs with flour, onion, herbs and spices.
Pour into a hot oiled pan, cover and cook on low heat until set underneath.
Flip and cook the second side, then cut into wedges.
Dice the tomatoes, cucumbers, onion and pepper very small.
Chop the parsley and chili.
Dress with lemon juice, vinegar, oil, salt and cumin just before serving.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and vinegar; it will thicken.
Add the water gradually, whisking until smooth and pourable.
Stir in crushed garlic, cumin, salt and chopped parsley.
Char the whole eggplants over a gas flame or under the grill, turning, until collapsed and soft.
Cool slightly, peel and drain the flesh in a colander.
Mash the flesh with tahini, crushed garlic, lemon juice, cumin and salt.
Serve drizzled with olive oil and parsley.
Grate or finely dice the cucumber and squeeze out excess water.
Stir into the yogurt with crushed garlic, dried mint and salt; chill before serving.
Slice the eggplants into rounds, salt them lightly and leave for 10 minutes; pat dry.
Fry in hot oil until golden on both sides; drain on paper.
Mix crushed garlic, chopped chili and pepper, vinegar and cumin.
Layer the eggplant in a dish and pour the dressing over; rest at least 30 minutes.
Boil the beetroots in their skins until tender, about 45 minutes.
Cool, peel and dice; slice the onion thinly.
Toss with vinegar, oil, salt and cumin.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender; peel and cube.
Chop the onion and parsley.
Toss the warm potatoes with the onion, parsley, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, black pepper and cumin.
Skin and bone the herring and flake the flesh.
Dice the tomatoes, onion and pepper.
Mix with the herring, lemon juice, oil and pepper.
Rinse the lupini beans if they are brined.
Toss with lemon juice, cumin, chili and a little salt.
Blend the chickpeas with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt.
Add water gradually until very smooth.
Spread on a plate and finish with olive oil and paprika.
Crush the garlic with the salt.
Fry the garlic briefly in the oil until fragrant, not brown.
Add vinegar, water, lemon juice and cumin; bring to a boil and remove from heat.
Blend or grate the tomatoes.
Fry crushed garlic in oil for 1 minute, add tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, water, cumin, chili and salt; simmer until thickened.
Stir in the vinegar at the end.
Crush the garlic.
Fry the garlic in the ghee until pale golden, add the ground coriander and stir 30 seconds; use immediately.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Whisk in the milk gradually and cook, whisking, until thick and smooth.
Season with salt, white pepper and nutmeg.
Peel the turnips and beetroot and cut into wedges.
Pack into a clean jar with the garlic and chilies.
Dissolve the salt in the water, add the vinegar and pour over the vegetables to cover.
Close the jar and keep at room temperature for about one week before eating; then refrigerate.
Cut the cauliflower into florets and boil in salted water for 5 minutes; drain well.
Beat the eggs with flour, crushed garlic, spices and salt into a thick batter.
Dip the florets in the batter and fry in hot oil until golden.
Drain on paper and serve with lemon or tahini.
Rinse the lentils; roughly chop the onion, carrots, tomato and potato.
Put the lentils, vegetables, garlic and water in a pot, bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer covered until the lentils and vegetables are very soft.
Blend until smooth, season with cumin, salt and pepper and stir in the butter.
Serve with lemon wedges and toasted bread.
Toast the vermicelli in the butter, stirring, until golden.
Add water, stock cube and tomato paste; bring to a boil.
Simmer until the vermicelli is tender; season and garnish with parsley.
Wash the chicken, put it in a pot with the water and bring to a boil; skim the foam well.
Add the onion, bay leaf, cardamom, cinnamon stick and peppercorns.
Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the chicken; add diced carrot, celery and tomato and simmer until tender.
Season with salt and serve the broth; use the chicken for another dish.
Boil the chicken with onion, bay leaf and cardamom, skimming, to make broth; reserve the chicken.
Strip the molokhia leaves from the stems, wash, dry well and mince very finely with a mezzaluna.
Bring 1.5 litres of broth to a boil, season and add the molokhia; stir and bring back just to the boil.
Fry crushed garlic in ghee until golden, add ground coriander and pour sizzling into the pot.
Serve at once with rice and the chicken (browned in the oven if liked).
Rub the rabbit pieces with lemon and salt and rinse.
Simmer the rabbit with onion, bay leaf and cardamom, skimming, until tender.
Mince the molokhia finely.
Boil 1.5 litres of the broth, add the molokhia and bring back to the boil.
Add the garlic and coriander ta'leya fried in ghee and serve with rice and the rabbit. Season with salt and black pepper.
Peel the shrimp; simmer the shells with onion in the water for 15 minutes and strain.
Mince the molokhia finely.
Fry the shrimp with half the garlic in oil for 2 minutes and set aside.
Boil the stock, add molokhia and the shrimp, and bring back just to the boil.
Fry the remaining garlic with coriander and cumin and pour over; serve with rice. Season with salt.
Rub the dried molokhia between the palms to a powder, removing any stems.
Bring the water and stock cube to a boil and whisk in the molokhia; simmer 10 minutes, whisking.
Fry garlic and coriander in ghee and add to the pot; season and serve.
Soak the split fava beans overnight and drain.
Cook the beans with half the garlic and the water until very soft.
Add the chopped herbs, leek, molokhia and chili and simmer 10 minutes.
Blend until smooth and season with cumin, coriander and salt.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until dark golden and spoon over the bissara with some of the oil.
Dice all the vegetables.
Soften the onion in butter, add tomato and tomato paste and cook 3 minutes.
Add water, stock cube, carrots and potato; simmer 15 minutes.
Add zucchini and peas and cook until tender; season.
Pick over and rinse the freekeh.
Soften the chopped onion in butter, add the freekeh and stir 2 minutes.
Add water and stock cube and simmer until the freekeh is tender.
Season and serve with lemon.
Chop the tomatoes, onion and garlic.
Soften onion and garlic in butter, add tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add water, stock cube and rice and simmer until the rice is very soft.
Blend smooth and season.
Dice the chicken and vegetables.
Toast the vermicelli in butter, remove; brown the chicken lightly in the same pot.
Add water and vegetables and simmer 15 minutes.
Return the vermicelli, cook until tender and season; serve with lemon.
Scrub the tripe well with lemon and salt and rinse several times.
Blanch for 10 minutes, discard the water and cut into pieces.
Simmer in fresh water with onions, bay leaf and cardamom until very tender, skimming.
Fry crushed garlic, add vinegar and cumin and stir into the pot; season with lemon, salt and pepper.
Rinse the rice and drain well.
Toast the vermicelli in the ghee until deep golden.
Add the rice and stir to coat; add boiling water and salt.
Cover and cook on very low heat until the water is absorbed; rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Rinse and drain the rice.
Coat in melted ghee for 2 minutes, add boiling salted water.
Cover and cook on low heat until absorbed, then rest 5 minutes.
Slice the onions thinly and fry in the oil until dark golden and crisp; drain and keep the oil.
Boil the brown lentils in salted water until just tender, about 20 minutes; drain.
Fry the vermicelli in 2 tablespoons of the onion oil, add the rice, lentils, cumin and salt, then boiling water; cover and cook 20 minutes.
Boil the macaroni in salted water until al dente and drain.
For the sauce, fry half the garlic in onion oil, add tomato paste, grated tomatoes, chili and salt; simmer 15 minutes and add 2 tablespoons vinegar.
For the dakka, crush the remaining garlic with cumin, add the ground coriander, the rest of the vinegar and a little water and bring to a boil.
Layer rice-lentils, macaroni and chickpeas; top with sauce, dakka and crispy onions.
Cook the lentils in 700 ml water for 15 minutes.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until deep brown; remove half for topping.
Add the rinsed rice, cumin, salt and the lentils with their liquid (topped up to cover by 1 cm); cook covered on low until done.
Serve topped with the reserved onions.
Boil the gizzards until tender (about 30 minutes) and chop; dice the livers.
Fry the chopped onion in half the ghee, add the beef and brown; add livers and gizzards and cook 5 minutes with the spices.
Add rinsed rice, stir, then pour in boiling water with the stock cube; cover and cook on low for 20 minutes.
Toast the almonds and pine nuts in the remaining ghee; plump the raisins in the same pan.
Fluff the rice and scatter the nuts and raisins on top.
Heat the oven to 180 °C and butter a clay or ovenproof dish.
Bring milk, water and stock cube to a boil.
Put the rinsed rice and salt in the dish, pour over the hot liquid and dot with butter.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes, pour over the cream and bake 25 more minutes until browned on top.
Chop the onion and dill.
Soften the onion in oil, add the rice and dill and stir 2 minutes.
Add boiling salted water, cover and cook on low until done.
Grate the tomatoes; chop the onion.
Fry the onion in oil, add tomato paste and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add rice, cumin, salt and water; cover and cook on low until tender.
Simmer the fish trimmings (or one small fish) in the water for 20 minutes and strain to make stock.
Fry the sliced onions in oil until very dark brown but not burnt.
Add the rice and spices and stir, then 700 ml hot fish stock; cover and cook on low until done.
Boil the chicken with one onion, cardamom and bay leaf to make broth; reserve the chicken.
Fry the second onion in butter, add rinsed freekeh and stir 3 minutes.
Add 900 ml broth, cover and cook until the freekeh is tender.
Place the chicken on top and brown in a hot oven for 15 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Boil the beef with onion, bay leaf and cardamom, skimming, until tender; keep the broth.
Cut the bread into pieces and toast in the oven with a little ghee until crisp.
Cook the rice with ghee and 550 ml broth.
Fry half the garlic in ghee, add vinegar and boil; separately fry the rest of the garlic, add tomato paste and grated tomatoes, and simmer to a sauce.
Moisten the bread with hot broth and the garlic vinegar, top with rice, then tomato sauce and the beef. Season the broth with salt and black pepper before using it.
Melt the butter, add peas and stir 2 minutes.
Add rinsed rice, boiling water and salt; cover and cook on low until done.
Fry the onion, add tomatoes and tomato paste and cook 5 minutes.
Add bulgur, salt and boiling water; cover and cook on low for 15 minutes; rest 5 minutes.
Cook the rinsed rice in the water until absorbed.
Add most of the milk and simmer, stirring often, until creamy.
Dissolve the corn starch in the remaining cold milk and stir in with the sugar; boil 2 minutes.
Add vanilla, pour into bowls and chill; top with cinnamon or nuts.
Soak the wheat overnight and boil in fresh water until the grains split and are tender (about 2 hours), or use pre-cooked wheat.
Heat the milk with the sugar.
Spoon the wheat into bowls, pour over hot milk and top with raisins, coconut, nuts and cinnamon.
Cut the zucchini into 8 cm lengths and core with a corer, leaving a thin wall.
Mix the rinsed rice with grated tomato, finely chopped onion and herbs, half the tomato paste, oil and spices.
Fill the zucchini three-quarters full to leave room for the rice to swell.
Arrange upright in a pot; pour over water with the stock cube and remaining tomato paste to come halfway up.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low until the rice is tender.
Core the small eggplants, leaving a thin wall; soak briefly in salted water.
Make the filling from rice, grated tomato, chopped onion, garlic, herbs, half the tomato paste, oil and spices.
Stuff the eggplants three-quarters full.
Arrange in a pot, add water mixed with the remaining tomato paste and salt.
Cover and simmer until tender.
Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds; keep the tops.
Mix the filling: rice, grated tomato, chopped onion and herbs, half the tomato paste, oil and spices.
Fill the peppers three-quarters full and replace the tops.
Stand them in a pot, add water with the remaining tomato paste and salt.
Cover and simmer until the rice is tender.
Blanch the vine leaves in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes and drain; trim the stems.
Mix the rice with grated tomato, finely chopped onion and herbs, oil and spices.
Place a teaspoon of filling on each leaf (shiny side down) and roll tightly, tucking in the sides.
Line the pot with the lamb chops or extra leaves, arrange the rolls in tight layers and weigh down with a plate.
Add water with the stock cube and lemon juice to just cover; simmer covered on low until the rice is cooked.
Core the cabbage and boil whole, peeling off the leaves as they soften; cut large leaves in half and trim the ribs.
Mix the rice with grated tomato, chopped onion, herbs, half the tomato paste, oil, cumin and caraway.
Roll each leaf around a line of filling into a finger-thick roll.
Pack in a pot with the garlic cloves between layers; add water with the remaining tomato paste and salt.
Weigh down with a plate, cover and simmer until tender.
Slice the tops off the tomatoes and scoop out the pulp; chop the pulp.
Mix the rice with half the pulp, onion, herbs, oil and seasoning.
Fill the tomatoes, replace the tops and arrange in a baking dish.
Add the remaining pulp and water, cover with foil and bake at 190 °C until the rice is tender.
Core the zucchini and eggplant, deseed the peppers and blanch the vine leaves.
Prepare one filling of rice, grated tomato, chopped onion, herbs, half the tomato paste, oil and spices.
Stuff the vegetables three-quarters full and roll the vine leaves.
Arrange vine leaves at the bottom and the vegetables upright on top.
Add water with stock cubes and remaining tomato paste; cover and simmer until all is tender.
Cut a slit to the centre of each onion and boil 8 minutes until the layers separate.
Prepare the rice filling with grated tomato, herbs, half the tomato paste, oil and seasoning.
Roll a little filling inside each onion layer.
Pack into a pot, add water with remaining tomato paste and pomegranate molasses.
Cover and simmer until tender.
Core the zucchini.
Mix the beef with rice, grated onion, allspice, salt and pepper.
Stuff the zucchini loosely.
Make a sauce of garlic fried in oil with tomato paste, grated tomatoes and water.
Lay the zucchini in the sauce, cover and simmer until tender.
Simmer the beef cubes with onion in the water until tender; keep the broth.
Trim the okra caps.
Fry garlic and coriander in ghee, add tomato paste and grated tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add okra, beef and 500 ml broth; simmer until the okra is tender (or bake in a clay pot).
Season and add lemon juice if liked.
Simmer the beef with half the onion until tender.
Top and cut the beans; dice the carrots.
Fry the remaining onion and garlic, add tomato paste and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add beans, carrots, beef and broth; simmer until tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Simmer the beef with half the onion until tender.
Dice the carrots.
Fry the remaining onion, add tomato paste and grated tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add peas, carrots, beef and broth and simmer until tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Simmer the beef with the onion until nearly tender.
Peel and cube the potatoes.
Make a sauce with garlic, tomato paste, tomatoes and spices.
Toss the potatoes in the oil, combine with the beef, sauce and broth in an oven dish and bake at 200 °C until the potatoes are tender.
Boil the beef until tender.
Cut all vegetables into large chunks.
Toss the vegetables with oil, garlic, tomato paste, grated tomatoes, salt and pepper.
Add the beef and broth in a deep tray and bake at 200 °C until the vegetables are soft and browned.
Simmer the beef with one onion until tender.
Wash and chop the spinach.
Fry the other onion and garlic in ghee with coriander, then add the spinach until wilted.
Add beef, broth, tomato paste and the rice (to thicken); simmer 15 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Peel the taro (wear gloves), cube and rinse well.
Blend the chard leaves and fresh coriander with a little water to a green paste.
Fry the garlic in ghee, add the green paste and cook 5 minutes.
Add the taro, water and stock cubes; simmer until the taro is tender and the sauce thickens.
Season and add lemon juice.
Simmer the beef with the onion until tender.
Trim the artichokes to hearts and keep in water with lemon juice.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour, then add broth and lemon juice.
Add the hearts, peas and beef and simmer until the artichokes are tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Soak the beans overnight, drain and boil in fresh water until tender.
Fry the onion and garlic, add tomato paste and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add beans, boiled meat if using and cooking liquid; simmer until thick. Season with cumin, salt and black pepper.
Soak the peas for 4 hours, drain and boil until tender.
Fry onion and garlic, add tomato paste and tomatoes.
Add the peas and some of their liquid and simmer until thick. Season with cumin and salt.
Slice the eggplant, salt, then fry until golden; fry the pepper strips too.
Fry the onion, garlic and chili (and beef if using), add tomato paste, tomatoes and spices and cook 10 minutes.
Layer eggplant, peppers and sauce in a tray; add vinegar.
Bake at 190 °C for 25 minutes.
Slice and lightly fry the zucchini in a little butter.
Brown the beef with the onion, salt and pepper.
Make a béchamel with the remaining butter, flour and milk; season with nutmeg and beat in the egg.
Layer zucchini and meat in a tray, cover with béchamel and cheese and bake at 200 °C until golden.
Trim the okra.
Fry onion, garlic and coriander in olive oil, add tomato paste and tomatoes.
Add okra and water and simmer until tender; finish with lemon. Season with salt.
Simmer the chicken pieces with one onion, cardamom and bay leaf for 25 minutes.
Fry the second onion, garlic and pepper, add tomato paste and tomatoes.
Add the chicken and 400 ml of its broth and simmer until the sauce thickens.
Mix the beef with one grated onion, parsley, breadcrumbs, egg and spices; knead well.
Roll into walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs in oil and set aside.
Fry the second onion and garlic, add tomato paste, tomatoes and water.
Add the meatballs and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Scrub the tongue and boil with onion, bay leaf and cardamom until tender.
Peel off the skin while warm and slice.
Make a tomato sauce with the second onion, garlic, paste and tomatoes; add some broth.
Simmer the slices in the sauce for 10 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.
Cut the liver into thin strips and the chili and pepper into slices.
Heat the oil until very hot; add the liver and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add garlic, chili and pepper, then cumin and black pepper, and cook 2 minutes more.
Season with salt off the heat (salting earlier toughens liver) and add lemon juice.
Clean the gizzards and simmer in the water with half the onion until tender.
Fry the remaining onion, pepper and garlic in oil.
Add the livers and cook 4 minutes, then the drained gizzards and spices.
Finish with lemon juice and salt.
Marinate the chicken with garlic, oil, spices and half the salt.
Slice potatoes, onions and tomatoes and layer in a tray with the remaining salt.
Pour over water mixed with tomato paste and place the chicken on top.
Cover and bake at 200 °C for 45 minutes, uncover and bake until browned.
Marinate the fish in garlic, lemon, cumin, salt and pepper.
Slice the potatoes, peppers, onions and tomatoes and layer in a tray with oil.
Lay the fish on top, add the water, cover and bake at 200 °C for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more.
Cut the fish into steaks and marinate with garlic, cumin, lemon and salt.
Fry the onions and peppers in oil, add tomato paste and tomatoes and cook 10 minutes.
Put half the sauce in a clay pot, add the fish and cover with the rest.
Bake at 200 °C until the fish is cooked. Sprinkle with ground coriander before baking.
Peel and devein the shrimp; marinate with garlic, cumin and lemon.
Cook onion, pepper and chili in oil; add tomato paste and tomatoes.
Combine with the shrimp in a clay pot and bake at 200 °C for 15 to 20 minutes. Season with salt.
Cut the beef into cubes and slice the onions.
Brown the beef in ghee, add the onions and cook until soft.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, spices and water; transfer to a clay pot.
Cover and bake at 170 °C until the meat is very tender.
Boil the macaroni in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet time; drain.
Brown the beef with chopped onion, tomato paste, allspice, salt and pepper.
Make a béchamel with butter, flour and milk; season with nutmeg; mix one egg and a quarter of the béchamel into the pasta.
Layer half the pasta, the meat, then the remaining pasta in a buttered tray.
Beat the second egg into the remaining béchamel, pour over and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake at 200 °C until golden on top.
Rinse the lentils and boil in the water until tender.
Fry onion and garlic, add the tomatoes and cumin.
Stir into the lentils and simmer 10 minutes; season.
Simmer the chickpeas in the water for 10 minutes.
Add diced tomato, cumin, chili and salt.
Serve hot in cups with lemon and coriander.
Soak whole dried fava beans for 2 to 3 days, changing the water, until small sprouts appear.
Boil the beans with the onion in the water until tender.
Season with cumin and salt and serve the broth and beans with lemon.
Simmer the lamb shanks with the onion until tender, skimming.
Trim the okra.
Fry garlic and coriander in ghee; add tomato paste and tomatoes.
Add okra, lamb and broth and simmer until tender. Season with salt and black pepper.
Slice and fry the eggplant; drain.
Cook a garlic tomato sauce for 10 minutes.
Layer eggplant, sauce and grated cheese in a dish and bake at 200 °C for 20 minutes. Season the sauce with salt and black pepper.
Boil and mash the potatoes with butter, milk, nutmeg and half the salt.
Brown the beef with onion, salt and pepper.
Spread half the mash in a tray, add the meat, cover with the rest of the mash.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle breadcrumbs and bake at 200 °C until golden.
Grate the onion and squeeze out the juice; chop the parsley finely.
Knead the meats with onion, parsley, garlic and spices for 5 minutes; chill 30 minutes.
Shape onto skewers or into fingers.
Brush with oil and grill over hot charcoal or a grill pan, turning, until cooked through.
Cut the lamb into 4 cm cubes with some fat.
Grate one onion over the meat, add spices and marinate at least 2 hours.
Thread onto skewers with onion and tomato pieces.
Grill over hot charcoal, basting with ghee, until browned.
Salt after grilling and serve with tahini and salad.
Finely chop the onion, peppers and parsley and squeeze excess liquid from the onion.
Mix the beef with the vegetables and spices.
Open each loaf (about 6 loaves in total) into a pocket and spread a thin, even layer of meat inside.
Brush the outside with melted ghee.
Bake at 220 °C on a tray, turning once, until the bread is crisp and the meat cooked (or cook in a pan pressed under a weight).
Slice the breasts horizontally into thin cutlets and pound lightly.
Marinate with garlic, lemon, salt, pepper and paprika for 15 minutes.
Coat in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Fry in hot oil until golden and cooked through, about 3 minutes per side.
Butterfly or quarter the chicken and slash the thick parts.
Blend the yogurt, lemon, garlic, grated onion, spices, salt and oil; marinate the chicken at least 2 hours.
Roast at 210 °C, skin up, until the juices run clear.
Grill for the last 5 minutes to crisp the skin.
Clean the pigeons inside and out.
Cook the freekeh in ghee with chopped onion and diced liver, then add water to half-cook it.
Stuff the pigeons loosely and sew or skewer shut.
Simmer the pigeons in water with onion, cardamom, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 minutes.
Brush with ghee and roast at 220 °C (or fry) until golden.
Rub the rabbit with lemon and salt and rinse.

Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold in; chill at least 4 hours.
Heat the cream with vanilla; whisk the yolks with 80 g sugar and stir in the cream.
Pour into ramekins and bake in a water bath at 150 °C until just set.
Chill, then sprinkle with the remaining sugar and caramelise with a torch or hot grill.
Boil the potatoes and blanch the green beans; cool.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard and salt.
Arrange lettuce, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, eggs, tuna and olives and dress.
Mix the flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt and cut in the cold butter.
Stir in the buttermilk just until the dough holds; fold twice and cut rounds.
Bake at 230 °C until tall and golden.
